text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.84% today, recovering from a sharp drop on November 18th (when the stock fell 3.8%) and clawing back to near last week's levels. The bounce follows a stabilization in oil prices—US crude is holding at $89.53 per barrel after earlier weakness—and comes as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East briefly resurfaced with reported attacks between Iran-backed forces and Saudi Arabia. While the immediate news doesn't eliminate the downside risk these tensions represent, the lack of a major supply disruption has allowed prices and the stock to settle.

The recovery also reflects growing structural tailwinds for energy companies: permitting reform just passed the Senate with backing from both AI and energy sectors, potentially easing development constraints, and long-term demand indicators remain supportive as data center electricity use is expected to double by 2030. These factors may be underpinning confidence in the sector even as near-term volatility persists.
